paragraphs: R. Chalafta, in Mishnah Taanit, chapter 2, mishnah 5, father of R. Yosi and R. Shimon. He lived in the Temple period and after the destruction. He saw Rabban Gamliel the Elder, as in Shabbat 115a, and Rabban Gamliel of Yavneh. He instituted a practice at Tzippori: Taanit 16b; Rosh Hashanah 27a. He is called Abba Chalafta: Sotah 34a. R. Yosi said, “Abba Chalafta concedes”—Bekhorot 26a. Rashi explains: “My father, whose name is Chalafta, concedes.” R. Yosi said, “When Abba Chalafta went to study Torah with R. Yochanan ben Nuri”; some say, “R. Yochanan ben Nuri with Abba Chalafta”: Bava Kamma 70a, near the end; Bava Batra 56b. Elazar ben Matya and Chananyah ben Chakhinai stood on the stones erected in the Jordan. R. Chananyah ben Teradyon and R. Meir were his colleagues. He is not mentioned elsewhere in the Mishnah. Whoever says that Chalafta of Kefar Chananyah was R. Yosi's father is mistaken, for the latter lived in his teacher's generation after the destruction, a student of R. Meir. In HaOreg, Shabbat 105b, R. Shimon ben Elazar speaks in the name of R. Chalafta bar Agra, who spoke in R. Yochanan ben Nuri's name. This is Rif's reading; our reading is Chilfa. Perhaps this was R. Yosi's father, and perhaps R. Yehudah bar Agra was his brother; see there. But this is not so: R. Yochanan ben Nuri studied from R. Chalafta, R. Yosi's father, as above; whereas R. Chalafta bar Agra spoke in R. Yochanan ben Nuri's name.
